text: How much EU funding did the AQUACOMBINE project receive?
gold_sql: SELECT ecMaxContribution FROM project WHERE acronym = 'AQUACOMBINE';
reference_answer: The AQUACOMBINE project received 9789883.64 in EU funding (its committed EC contribution).
notes: Grounded on project table. Acronym AQUACOMBINE verified unique (n=1); acronyms are not globally unique in this DB (e.g. AQUATIC appears twice), so a verified-unique key was chosen. EU funding = ecMaxContribution per schema note (not totalCost). Gold executed this pass -> single row 9789883.64.

text: How many times did organisations take part in Horizon 2020 projects as unfunded partners?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS participation_count FROM organization WHERE role = 'partner';
reference_answer: Organisations took part in Horizon 2020 projects as unfunded partners 7658 times; these are the MSCA partner participations, none of which carry an EC contribution.
notes: Grounded on organization table, single table, no join. Value note: role 'partner (MSCA, unfunded)' - 'unfunded partner' maps to role='partner' only via the note, not from the column name (other partner-ish roles exist: thirdParty, internationalPartner). Cross-check: partner slice = 7658 rows, 0 with non-null ecContribution, matching the note's 'NULL for all 7,658 partner rows'. Gold executed this pass -> single row 7658. Watch-item (not a documented trap): a model reading 'unfunded' might filter ecContribution IS NULL instead, returning 7800 (7658 partners + 142 others) - a wrong answer, not scored as a trap since this is typed value-grounded. sql_comparison=set.

text: How many projects did each European Research Council grant scheme fund?
gold_sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC%' GROUP BY fundingScheme ORDER BY fundingScheme
reference_answer: Among the ERC grant schemes, Starting Grants (ERC-STG) fund the most projects at 2771, followed by Consolidator Grants (ERC-COG) at 2254 and Advanced Grants (ERC-ADG) at 1584. Proof of Concept schemes account for 967 (ERC-POC) and 158 (ERC-POC-LS), while Synergy Grants (ERC-SyG) cover 99 and ERC-LVG just 5.
notes: Grounded on project table, single table, no join. Scoped to ERC scheme family via fundingScheme LIKE 'ERC%' (56 schemes total; ERC family = 7). GROUP BY without ranking -> L2. ORDER BY fundingScheme is display-only (no LIMIT), sql_comparison=set. Gold executed this pass -> 7 rows: ERC-ADG 1584, ERC-COG 2254, ERC-LVG 5, ERC-POC 967, ERC-POC-LS 158, ERC-STG 2771, ERC-SyG 99. Not value-grounded: ERC is a scheme-name prefix, not a schema value note. Discrimination risk noted: tail schemes ERC-LVG/ERC-POC-LS are easy to miss.

text: How many projects classified under machine learning, including any of its subfields, are coordinated by organisations based in Spain?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS n_projects FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE o.role = 'coordinator' AND o.country = 'ES' AND e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/machine learning%';
reference_answer: 156 Horizon 2020 projects classified under machine learning or one of its subfields are coordinated by organisations based in Spain.
notes: Rewritten from the original sql-08, which required the exact leaf euroSciVocTitle='machine learning' (107) without the question text signalling exact-leaf scope. Grounded on project JOIN organization JOIN euroscivoc (both on projectID=id), 2 joins / 3 tables -> L3 multi-join. Vocabulary check this pass: 'machine learning' is an interior node with 6 subfields (deep learning, reinforcement learning, unsupervised/supervised/semisupervised learning, transfer learning); ALL paths containing 'machine learning' lie in this AI subtree, so euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/machine learning%' matches the node and its descendants exactly, no over-match. Question text says 'including any of its subfields' to pin the subtree reading. Role filter role='coordinator' (self-describing enum), country='ES'. Fan-out check: COUNT(*)=157 vs COUNT(DISTINCT p.id)=156 (one project carries two ML-subtree classifications), so DISTINCT is required. Gold executed this pass -> single row 156. Discrimination: exact-leaf-only reading gives 107, now a genuine model error given the question wording. sql_comparison=set (scalar).

text: In total, how much EU funding did organisations based in Germany receive across Horizon 2020?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(ecContribution) AS total_eu_funding FROM organization WHERE country = 'DE'
reference_answer: Organisations based in Germany received 10097888325.89 in EU funding across all their Horizon 2020 participations, summed from each organisation's own EC contribution.
notes: Trap type: totalCost/ecMaxContribution-across-join double-count. Gold sums per-org organization.ecContribution WHERE country='DE' (single table, no join) -> 10097888325.89, executed this pass. WRONG QUERY (executed this pass, runs clean, different answer): SELECT SUM(p.ecMaxContribution) FROM organization o JOIN project p ON o.projectID=p.id WHERE o.country='DE' -> 160168284153.26. The near-miss: schema says ecMaxContribution is THE 'EU funding' column, but explicitly warns 'Never SUM it across a join to organization (it repeats per org row)'; a careless model joins project to apply the country filter and inflates ~16x (result exceeds the whole ~80B H2020 budget). Correct per-country funding lives in organization.ecContribution. DE=Germany is general knowledge, not a value note -> trap, not value-grounded. sql_comparison=set (scalar).

text: In a project where a group of robots collectively assembled objects the way certain colony-dwelling animals build up their homes piece by piece, the robot that laid each piece could only sense a small region around itself at any moment. What hardware limitation forced its perception to stay so narrow?
reference_answer: The block-placing robot in this project - the BuilderBot - had to keep its field of view very small in order to stop its onboard CPU from overheating. As a result it could see only a few of the Stigmergic Blocks at a time, which limited the complexity of the structures it could build and the reliability of the building process.
notes: Seed: 846009 SRoCS (the only project in the euroscivoc 'swarm robotics' cluster, n=5, whose report documents a block-placing robot with a deliberately narrow field of view). L1 detail: the reason (field of view kept small to prevent CPU overheating) lives only in report_text.workPerformed, not in any stored column. Gold = seed only; |gold|=1 -> L1. Adjudication: pooled k=20 on the final wording surfaced 40 distinct projects across the four conditions; all 39 non-seed candidates OUT - industrial pick-and-place/assembly (PICKPLACE, LABOR, SYMBIO-TIC, GROW, VisionBot), space/planetary assembly (PRO-ACT, PULSAR, FACILITATORS), real-insect biology (ANTSolve, Ceratina, EMERG-ANT, Vision-In-Flight, HIVEOPOLIS), and swarm/collective robotics without the FOV-overheating fact (DEMIURGE, BROS, gAIa, SWARMs, CyBioSys); none describes a swarm-construction robot whose view was narrowed to prevent processor overheating. Completeness sweep (fact-based, wording-independent): run_sql over project.objective LIKE '%swarm%' AND (build|construct|assembl) -> 22 rows, only SRoCS is a swarm-robotics construction system; run_sql over report_text (workPerformed/summary/finalResults) LIKE '%overheat%' -> 68 rows, all battery/server/cooling/LED thermal projects, none a robot field-of-view constraint. No additional gold. term_style=paraphrase (reviewer WARN): the question avoids the answer terms (CPU, overheating) and the seed's key vocabulary (field of view; 'nest building behavior of social insects' rendered as 'colony-dwelling animals building up their homes'). On this final wording SRoCS is found by dense (rank 2), hybrid (1) and hybrid_rerank (1) but only drops to lexical rank 5 (it was lexical rank 1 under exact-term phrasing) - residual lexical overlap on generic robotics vocabulary keeps the paraphrase label borderline rather than clean dense-only evidence. index_fingerprint be84cbad9182 (n_vectors 190248, bge-base-en-v1.5).

text: Which Horizon 2020 project is working to commercialize a bioartificial liver in which a bioreactor filled with a human liver cell line is temporarily connected to an end-stage liver disease patient's circulation to replace liver function and bridge the patient to a transplant?
reference_answer: The BALXPAND project, run by the SME Hep-Art. It concerns the HepaRG-AMC-BAL, a bioartificial liver built from a bioreactor embedded with the human liver cell line HepaRG that is temporarily connected to an end-stage liver disease patient's circulation to replace liver function and bridge the patient to a transplant (or support liver restoration until transplantation becomes superfluous).

text: Which project set out to understand how substances that occur naturally in some of the plants eaten by grass-fed sheep and cattle can rid the animals of the worms living in their digestive tracts, now that the usual medicines have largely stopped working against them?
reference_answer: The project is TANWORM ("How do tannins kill parasitic worms?"), which set out to explain the previously unknown way that condensed tannins - bioactive compounds found in certain forage plants - act against the gastrointestinal nematode parasites of grazing sheep and cattle. Using highly purified tannin molecules it studied how the tannins bind to the nematodes and how tannin polymer size affects that binding, and it used transcriptomics and biochemical experiments to identify the biological pathways disrupted in the worms - an alternative to the small number of synthetic drugs to which these parasites have become widely resistant.
notes: Seed: 798983 TANWORM, the unique corpus project studying how a natural plant compound (condensed tannins, present in some bioactive forages) acts against the gastrointestinal nematode parasites of grazing sheep and cattle, as an alternative to synthetic anthelmintics the worms have grown resistant to. L1 identify: the work is described from the seed's free-text objective and the answer names the project; the question contains neither the acronym (TANWORM) nor the title, and deliberately omits the answer's key vocabulary. Gold = seed only; |gold|=1 -> L1. Re-verified on the final (reworded) wording; an earlier wording ('natural compounds in pasture plants combat the parasitic gut worms of grazing farm animals...') was re-run after edit and its results discarded. Pooled k=20 on the final wording surfaced 42 distinct projects; all 41 non-seed candidates OUT. Individually adjudicated OUTs: 656347 GUTWORM (human whipworm immunology), 773431 RELACS / 774340 Organic-PLUS (broad organic-input phase-out, not a plant-compound-vs-worm study), 862829 AVANT / 101036768 NeoGiANT / 867461 INFarm / 773436 HealthyLivestock (alternatives to ANTIBIOTICS/antimicrobials, target bacteria not worms), 101019223 DRUGSBUGS / 815628 HELP / 846873 SchiSTOP (human helminth drug/therapy work, synthetic, not livestock plant compounds), 747676 IDRAM (synthetic ivermectin uptake/resistance - the resistant-drug side, not the plant-compound alternative), 635408 Paragone (vaccines for animal parasites), 866530 RuMinimum / 101000213 HoloRuminant / 955374 MonoGutHealth (ruminant/monogastric microbiome), plus feed/grass/livestock-production, vaccine, genomics, humanities and off-topic projects (MarkEfficiency, HEALTHSTOCK, NanoFEED, GO-GRASS, Inno4Grass, SustainSAHEL, AncestralWeave, MetaPlat, BOAR, OvaVAx, BGV1, SchmaVirusVacDiag, EXL01, HerbaRice, reMEDIAL NATURE, TRANSCORP, etc.) - none is a natural-plant-compound anthelmintic for livestock gut worms. Completeness sweep (non-embedding, wording-independent): run_sql over project.objective for (tannin|bioactive forage|plant extract|plant secondary metabolite|phytochemical) AND (nematode|helminth|anthelmintic|parasitic worm|gastrointestinal parasite) -> 2 rows (TANWORM + 101024269 BISEM, which is western-corn-rootworm/maize plant-defense ecology, OUT); run_sql over objective for (nematode|helminth|anthelmintic|parasitic worm) AND (ruminant|sheep|cattle|grazing|livestock|pasture) -> 4 rows (TANWORM + IDRAM/Paragone/RELACS, all OUT); euroscivoc 'parasitology' leaf -> 9 projects (leishmaniasis/malaria/trypanosome/microsporidia/foodborne, all OUT; TANWORM is not even under this leaf).
